content.text: dysrhythmias, severe hypotension, convulsions and CNS depression or coma; QRS axis or width chgs are key signs of toxicity. Get an ECG, start ♡ monitoring and observe for ± six hrs; a limb-lead QRS of 0.10 seconds or more may best show severity; give IV sodium bicarb to keep serum pH @ 7.45 to 7.55. Type 1A and 1C antiarrhythmics are generally contraindicated.
CYP2D6 inhibitors (eg, quinidine, cimetidine) can make a pt stable on a TCA abruptly toxic; the combo may need lower doses of the TCA or the other drug.
